# Amazon Selling Partner
Skills for managing an Amazon seller account via SP-API, through the Amazon Selling Partner Connector (MCP). Write actions are always human-in-the-loop (drafted for your approval).
## Connector
The bundled `.mcp.json` registers the Amazon Selling Partner Connector (MCP server) at `https://sellingpartner-ai.amazon.com/mcp`. You authorize access through the standard Seller Central OAuth consent flow; the assistant can only use tools allowed by your Seller Central roles. Write actions are drafted for your approval.

- **invite-secondary-users** — guide the account admin to grant AI-agent access to secondary users via Seller Central Manage Agents (advisory; UI action).
- **support-case-helper** — route the seller to Amazon Seller Support and prepare a clean, PII-free case summary; never submits without explicit confirmation.

When you use these skills, the assistant sends requests to the Amazon Selling Partner Connector (MCP) at (`https://sellingpartner-ai.amazon.com/mcp`) over an authenticated connection:
- **What is sent:** the tool calls the skills make on your behalf (e.g. requests for your inventory, sales/traffic analytics, listing status, or a drafted listing/price change) and the parameters those calls need (such as your Merchant Token / marketplace and the SKU/ASIN in question). Your prompt text is processed by your AI assistant per its own terms.
- **What comes back:** your Amazon business data (inventory, analytics, listing details) that the gateway returns for the calls you approved.
- **Authorization & scope:** access is granted through the Seller Central OAuth consent flow and is limited to the tools your Seller Central roles allow. Write actions are never executed without your explicit approval.

# Data Kiosk MCP Server
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants like Claude Desktop to interact with Amazon's Data Kiosk API for analyzing seller and vendor data.
**This MCP server example runs locally in your test environment and provides a foundation for development and experimentation. Developers utilizing this sample solution are responsible for its implementation, usage patterns, and ensuring compliance with Amazon's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) and Data Protection Policy (DPP).**
0729.mov
## Overview
This MCP server provides a bridge between AI assistants and Amazon's Data Kiosk API, allowing for powerful analytics capabilities through natural language conversations. It enables users to:
- Query Sales and Traffic data for Amazon sellers
- Analyze Economics and Profitability metrics
- Examine Vendor Analytics data
- Build and execute GraphQL queries
- Monitor query processing
- Download and analyze query results
## Architecture
The project is structured as a monorepo with three packages:
1. **common**: Shared utilities and base functionality
- Authentication with Amazon Selling Partner API
- Base API interaction
- GraphQL query helpers
- Utility functions
2. **seller-server**: MCP server for Amazon Seller Analytics
- Sales and Traffic analytics tools
- Economics data tools
- Example query builders
3. **vendor-server**: MCP server for Amazon Vendor Analytics
- Sourcing view analytics
- Manufacturing view analytics
- Example query builders
## Prerequisites
- Node.js v16 or higher
- An Amazon Seller Central or Vendor Central account with Data Kiosk access
- Amazon Selling Partner API credentials:
- Client ID
- Client Secret
- Refresh Token
## Installation
1. Clone the repository:
```
git clone https://github.com/amzn/selling-partner-api-samples.git
cd use-cases/amazon-data-kiosk-mcp-server
```
1. Install dependencies:
```
npm install
```
1. Build all packages:
```
npm run build
```
## Configuration
### Environment Variables
Set the following environment variables:
```
DATA_KIOSK_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
DATA_KIOSK_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
DATA_KIOSK_REFRESH_TOKEN=your_refresh_token
DATA_KIOSK_BASE_URL=https://sellingpartnerapi-na.amazon.com
DATA_KIOSK_OAUTH_URL=https://api.amazon.com/auth/o2/token
DATA_KIOSK_API_VERSION=2023-11-15
```

title: Preparing for the 2026 Holiday Shopping Season with Amazon's Selling Partner plugin & Ads MCP
snippet:
The holidays are fast approaching and as sellers prepare for the busy 2026 season, they now have two new AI tools that don’t just answer questions but actively help manage holiday operations and advertising: the Amazon Selling Partner plugin and the Amazon Ads MCP Server. Used together in AWS Quick, they let sellers check inventory, adjust campaigns, optimize listings, act on performance data, and more.

Before diving into the individual tools, it’s important to understand [AWS Quick](https://aws.amazon.com/quick/)—the AI companion that serves as the home base for these integrations. AWS Quick creates documents, spreadsheets, runs deep research, and connects to your email, calendar, and files. More importantly for sellers, it lets you use the Selling Partner Plugin and Ads MCP Server in a unified workflow—asking questions about inventory in one breath and adjusting ad campaigns in the next.

Also announced at Accelerate 2026, the [Selling Partner plugin](https://developer.amazonservices.com/amazon-selling-partner-plugin) is currently in beta for US stores. It connects AI assistants like AWS Quick and Anthropic’s Claude directly to your Seller Central data, giving you conversational access to manage areas like:
- **Product listings**: Review, audit, and optimize your catalog in natural language
- **Inventory levels:** Monitor stock and flag low-inventory ASINs before they go out of stock during peak demand
- **Sales data**: Analyze performance trends and identify your top-performing holiday products
Instead of clicking through Seller Central dashboards, you can simply ask, “Which of my top ASINs are at risk of stocking out?,” and get an answer in seconds. No more manually clicking through multiple Seller Central tabs to piece together the answer yourself. You can make live decisions during peak days without missing a beat. Connect AI agents to AWS Partner Central with the MCP
Server
The Partner Central agents MCP Server provides Partner Central tools through the Model Context
Protocol (MCP), enabling your AI agents and tools to discover and interact with opportunity
management, customer insights, and funding programs through natural language.
The server handles authentication, session management, and human-in-the-loop approval for
write operations maintaining control while streamlining workﬂows.
Overview
The Partner Central agents MCP Server is a fully managed, AWS-hosted service that connects MCP-
compatible AI clients to the Partner Central agents. It uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTPS with SigV4
authentication and supports Server-Sent Events (SSE) for real-time streaming responses.
The server supports multi-turn conversations, ﬁle attachments for document analysis, and a built-
in approval workﬂow that requires your explicit consent before any write operation executes.

The Partner Central Agent MCP Server exposes two MCP tools: sendMessage for all agent
interactions, and getSession for retrieving session state. All Partner Central operations —
opportunity queries, funding applications, document analysis — are handled through natural
language via sendMessage.

It connects to your local ﬁles and the tools you use
every day and builds an understanding of your business over time. By bringing the AWS Partner
Central agents into Quick through the Partner Central agents MCP (Model Context Protocol)
Server, you pair AWS co-sell and funding capabilities with your own customer context in one place,
then apply ready-made AWS Partner skills to move faster. The value grows as you adapt it to your
workﬂow by plugging in your own tools, data, and processes so it reﬂects how your team runs.
